issues.description: Method acceptSupplyDelivery: the problem statement (UML and textual description) declares acceptSupplyDelivery with four parameters including a supplier name (acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity)), but the template/example call and the provided solution implement and use a three-parameter signature (acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity)). This discrepancy between the spec and the code will confuse students about which signature to implement and may lead to compilation or test mismatches or incorrect implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the acceptSupplyDelivery signature consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fixes: (A) Update the problem statement UML and the textual description to specify acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (remove the supplierName parameter) to match the template example and the solution; OR (B) If supplier information is required pedagogically, change the template Main example and the SealSaloon implementation to accept (String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and update all references. Ensure the UML, problem text, example calls, and the SealSaloon implementation use the same parameter count, types, and order.
